CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Semarang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Semarang.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Human Rights is a set of rights inherent to the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and constitutes His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept.
7. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
8. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
9. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society.
10. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are naturally inherent in and inseparable from human beings, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.
Letter b What is meant by "The principle of non-discrimination" is that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter c What is meant by "The principle of gender equality and justice" is that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter d What is meant by "The principle of justice and legal certainty" is that which contains the understanding that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal treatment as well as to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law.
Letter e What is meant by "The principle of benefit" is that which contains the understanding that the regulation of women's empowerment policies must provide the greatest benefit for the welfare of society.
Letter f What is meant by "The principle of participation" is that which contains the understanding that the entire process of policy formation and implementation must take into account the active participation of all components of society so as to obtain equal benefits in all fields of development and life.
Letter g What is meant by "The principle of accountability" is that which concerns that the implementation of women's empowerment must be accountable and constitutes part of the accountability of government implementation.
Letter h What is meant by "The principle of inclusion" is the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that can hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.

STRATEGY FOR WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION
Article 23
(1) Women's Empowerment and Protection is implemented by integrating gender mainstreaming and gender-disaggregated data based on laws and regulations.
-12- (2) Women's Empowerment and Protection is implemented through working groups and/or integrated services established by Mayor's Decree.
(3) Women's Empowerment and Protection is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection.

Article 25
(1) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning as referred to in Article 24 letter a, shall be implemented through:
a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of program and activity planning with related Regional Apparatus; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
(2) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning shall be implemented based on minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
(3) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection, shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning.

CHAPTER VIII
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 29
(1) Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection functions as the leading sector in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
(2) Further provisions regarding the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 13
(1) Women's Empowerment in the field of law through:
   a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law with communication, information, and education services; and
   b. facilitating access to and services for legal consultation as well as gender-responsive legal aid.
(2) Women's Empowerment in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX
PARTICIPATION
Article 30
(1) The community, community groups/community organizations, business sector, academics, and/or other professional groups may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. cooperation;
b. synergy;
c. provision of communication, information and education media regarding Women's Empowerment and Protection; and
d. active role in the fulfillment of women's rights through social responsibility.
(3) Further provisions regarding participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

DRAFT REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG CITY
NUMBER 7 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

Letter a Sufficiently clear.
-21- Letter b What is meant by basic rights of workers includes:
a. basic right to obtain decent wages.
b. right to obtain equal opportunity and treatment from the company without discrimination.
c. right to obtain work training to improve and develop work competence.
d. right to perform work according to the determined time.
e. right to labor placement.
f. right to obtain protection for occupational health and safety.
g. right to obtain welfare through labor social security.
h. right to participate in trade unions or labor unions.
i. right to obtain leave: at least 12 working days after the employee has worked for one year continuously.
j. right to rest: workers after working four hours continuously, obtain rest opportunity for a minimum of half an hour.
k. right to maternity leave, miscarriage and menstrual leave specifically for female workers/laborers:
Female workers/laborers are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who experience miscarriage are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who during menstruation feel pain and notify the employer, are not obligated to work on the first and second day during menstruation.
l. right to perform worship.
m. right to conduct work strikes.
n. right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or dismissal.
o. right to appropriate opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

ELUCIDATION
OF
DRAFT REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG CITY
NUMBER 7 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

ELUCIDATION
OF
DRAFT REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG CITY
NUMBER 7 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

Female workers/laborers who experience miscarriage are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who during menstruation feel pain and notify the employer, are not obligated to work on the first and second day during menstruation.
l. right to perform worship.
m. right to conduct work strikes.
n. right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or dismissal.
o. right to appropriate opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

o. right to appropriate opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

Letter a What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are naturally inherent in and inseparable from human beings, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.

Letter f What is meant by "The principle of participation" is that which contains the understanding that the entire process of policy formation and implementation must take into account the active participation of all components of society so as to obtain equal benefits in all fields of development and life.
Letter g What is meant by "The principle of accountability" is that which concerns that the implementation of women's empowerment must be accountable and constitutes part of the accountability of government implementation.
Letter h What is meant by "The principle of inclusion" is the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that can hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.

NUMBER 7 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

Female workers/laborers who during menstruation feel pain and notify the employer, are not obligated to work on the first and second day during menstruation.

o. right to appropriate opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

NUMBER 7 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

Article 14
Letter a Sufficiently clear.
-21- Letter b What is meant by basic rights of workers includes:
a. basic right to obtain decent wages.
b. right to obtain equal opportunity and treatment from the company without discrimination.
c. right to obtain work training to improve and develop work competence.
d. right to perform work according to the determined time.
e. right to labor placement.
f. right to obtain protection for occupational health and safety.
g. right to obtain welfare through labor social security.
h. right to participate in trade unions or labor unions.
i. right to obtain leave: at least 12 working days after the employee has worked for one year continuously.
j. right to rest: workers after working four hours continuously, obtain rest opportunity for a minimum of half an hour.
k. right to maternity leave, miscarriage and menstrual leave specifically for female workers/laborers:
Female workers/laborers are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who experience miscarriage are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who during menstruation feel pain and notify the employer, are not obligated to work on the first and second day during menstruation.
l. right to perform worship.
m. right to conduct work strikes.
n. right to obtain severance pay in the event of termination of employment or dismissal.
o. right to appropriate opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if it must be done during working hours.

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 29
(1) Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection functions as the leading sector in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
(2) Further provisions regarding the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with statutory provisions.

CHAPTER IX
PARTICIPATION
Article 30
(1) The community, community groups/community organizations, business sector, academics, and/or other professional groups may participate in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. cooperation;
b. synergy;
c. provision of communication, information and education media regarding Women's Empowerment and Protection; and
d. active role in the fulfillment of women's rights through social responsibility.
(3) Further provisions regarding participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Mayor Regulation.

Article 25
(1) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning as referred to in Article 24 letter a, shall be implemented through:
a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of program and activity planning with related Regional Apparatus; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
(2) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning shall be implemented based on minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
(3) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection, shall be coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning.

CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improved services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal status in law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equal status for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, under certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

Letter a What is meant by "The principle of respect for human rights" contains the understanding that the Republic of Indonesia recognizes and upholds human rights and fundamental human freedoms as rights that are naturally inherent in and inseparable from human beings, which must be protected, respected, and upheld for the enhancement of human dignity, welfare, happiness, and intelligence as well as justice.
Letter b What is meant by "The principle of non-discrimination" is that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter c What is meant by "The principle of gender equality and justice" is that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter d What is meant by "The principle of justice and legal certainty" is that which contains the understanding that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal treatment as well as to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law.
Letter e What is meant by "The principle of benefit" is that which contains the understanding that the regulation of women's empowerment policies must provide the greatest benefit for the welfare of society.
Letter f What is meant by "The principle of participation" is that which contains the understanding that the entire process of policy formation and implementation must take into account the active participation of all components of society so as to obtain equal benefits in all fields of development and life.
Letter g What is meant by "The principle of accountability" is that which concerns that the implementation of women's empowerment must be accountable and constitutes part of the accountability of government implementation.
Letter h What is meant by "The principle of inclusion" is the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is carried out by inviting and involving all people with various diversities of abilities, backgrounds, characteristics, status, conditions, ethnicity, culture and others as well as facilitating special needs based on such diversity and eliminating barriers that can hinder the equality of every woman in obtaining her rights.
